The smartest parenting trick nobody talks about: stop telling them, and let them overhear. 👂

Kids tune out lectures. But they never miss what they overhear. 🎧

Esther is seven, and she's shy. One night on the stairs, she hears Mom say, "She's so shy…" And it bounces around her head for days. 😔

So Mom tries something new:
1️⃣ Say the good, where she can hear it. "Esther ordered her own food today. She's braver than she thinks." (Esther is pretending not to listen 😉)
2️⃣ Only say what's true.
3️⃣ Take your worries to God in prayer, not to the kitchen table where little ears can hear. 🙏

In one study, two-year-olds learned new words just as well by overhearing them as when spoken to directly (Akhtar, Jipson & Callanan, Child Development, 2001).

The night before the cross, Jesus prayed for us. "I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word." John 17:20 (ESV) ❤️ We get to overhear what Jesus says about us.

Years later, Mom asks if she's sure she can do it. Esther smiles: "Sure." Because she's braver than she thinks. ❤️

Make sure what they overhear is love. It becomes the loudest voice in your child's head.
